notes: §1985:XII.3.4 GR10: text words a REPLACE inserts "are placed in the source program according to the rules for reference format", and GR9 judges the program only after all COPY and REPLACE processing (kb/Work PB5313, landed). ApplyReplacements writes pseudo-text-2 at the position of the text it replaces (its origin, which diagnostics and EXCEPTION-LOCATION name) but lays it out where it was written (OriginWriter.AppendLaidOut, OriginSpan.Layout), and AreaPlacementPass judges whether a token begins its line from the RESULTANT token stream and the area it begins in at its laid-out place (FixedFormAreas.PlacementAt over ReferenceFormatMap.AreaAt). So RA3 (pseudo-text-2 puts P2 in area A of a line of its own) compiles and prints A B D C (witness pb5313-replace-introduced-line-in-area-a). The determination for REPLACE is COPY's (§1985:XII.2.4 GR9: a word of pseudo-text-2 "begins in the same area of the resultant program as it appears in pseudo-text-2"): the same GR10 sentence stands beside that rule in the COPY statement, so the compiler keeps the area each word was written in rather than moving it; RA5 (a single P2. written in area B replacing XXX) is therefore refused (COBOL3734, 'begins in area B, where pseudo-text-2 writes it'). The second sentence (no added spaces) holds (RA6).

next.reason: 1985: "are placed in the source program according to the rules for reference format. (See page IV-41, Reference Format.)"; 2023: "shall be in logical free-form reference format. Text-words inserted ... are placed in accordance with the rules of free-form reference format". The extra-space rule is the same; the assumed space at line end is now NOTE 2. But inserted words now follow free-form rules, not the 1985 (fixed) reference format with its areas.
